# name: # Inputs that must raise a parse error. `expected` uses the literal token
# "ERROR" (optionally ":code" for a specific error code) to indicate that
# An unbound namespace prefix violates Namespaces in XML 1.0, which is a
# SEPARATE spec from XML 1.0 well-formedness: `<foo:b/>` is a well-formed
# XML document. The check is therefore opt-in via `strictNamespaces`; the
# default (accepting) behaviour is pinned in namespaces.tsv.
# A namespace name is a URI reference (Namespaces in XML 1.0 §2), and a URI
# reference cannot contain white space. Attribute-value normalisation
# (§3.3.3) turns a literal line break in the declaration into a space
# first, so both spellings land on the same error.
# Error templates must interpolate. The `msg` column pins the rendered
# text, so a template that reverts to a literal `$fsrc` / `$openname`
# placeholder fails here instead of shipping.

msg: closing tag does not match opening tag
closing tag </c> does not match opening tag <b>
